At small orders (256, 512) A in C is faster than the Python variant B: there $M$ is comparable to $|G|$ (for groups of order 256 with $d=6$ at $n=5$ $M=1554>255$), and Python has a fixed overhead per group. At order 2187 B is 30 times faster than A in C, and hundreds of times faster than numpy.

Rips-type family (gap/xcheck_fam.g) · $2^{40}$–$2^{107}$ · 4 · 5 · 380–2330 · 340 · 1.7–9 s per group

For the group of order $3^{494}$ the indices $\log_3|\Delta/\Delta^n|=59, 321, 1430$ ($n=2,3,4$) agreed modulo $3^{19}$ and over $\mathbb Z$. On the 394 tested elements (pcgs of layers 2–4) $D_n=\gamma_n$ for $n\le4$, consistent with Passi's theorem ($D_4=\gamma_4$ for odd $p$).

The reference is the answers of dimsub.py (kept with it, in a separate repository). Compared level by level: $|D_n|$, $|\gamma_n|$, equal, the set of extra elements, index_logp, and certified where it was computed in both.

$|D_n|$, $|\gamma_n|$, the extra elements, the certificates and the indices $\log_p[\Delta:\Delta^n+p^E\Delta]$ agree. In full mode, B on 1 425 groups (almost all elementary abelian or close to it, $M>500$) was stopped by the rank ceiling and compared on the prefix of levels. In fast mode this happened for 29 groups of order 256 with $d=6$. A was compared in full.

Variant B from a presentation (gap/export_pres.g → py/magnus_pres.py), all elements of each group tested: orders 64, 128, 243, 729, 512 (survivors), 2187 (sample): 6 007 groups, 17 140 levels, 0 differences, indices included. Separately: 20 groups of order 64 with the exact HNF over $\mathbb Z$ (--exact) and 5 groups of order 2187 with $n_{\max}=4<\mathrm{cls}+1$ (a check of the weight cut-off): 0 differences.

Cross-check with an independent implementation of the same method (unpublished; dictionaries of monomials, explicit enumeration of the pairs $u,v$, the relations of $G$ plus all commutators of weight 4).
Their code on our groups (scripts/xcheck_independent.py; relations and words from our export): the same 6 007 groups and 17 140 levels, 0 differences, indices included.
$D_5\cap\Omega_1(\gamma_3\cap M_5)=1$ in all 14 groups, as in theirs.
$D_4\cap\Omega_1(\gamma_3\cap M_4)$ has rank 1 exactly for $2^{84}$, $2^{90}$, $2^{107}$ and is trivial for the rest, as in theirs.

$\alpha=[e_0,e_1]^{32}[e_0,e_2]^{64}[e_1,e_2]^{128}\in D_4$ for $2^{84}$ and $2^{90}$; for $2^{107}$ and two other groups with $\alpha\ne1$, $\alpha\notin D_4$; for the rest $\alpha=1$. All as in theirs.

The exactness certificate ($p^{E-1}A_n^+\subseteq J_n+p^EA_n^+$) passes in all 42 cases. Therefore the memberships modulo $2^{30}$ are exact here, and $D_4(Q)\ne1$ for $2^{84}$, $2^{90}$ and $2^{107}$ is proved by computation, not merely a "candidate modulo $2^{30}$".
